name: Barr Emerger
imitates: John Barr's Baetis emerger; it sits in or just under the film, imitating a small mayfly shedding its shuck during blue-winged olive hatches.

steps.text: Attach the thread and wrap a base back about halfway down the bend.
Peel ten or twelve fibers from a prepared brown spade hackle and tie them in at the bend without flaring them, as they imitate the shuck rather than a tail.
Wrap forward over the butts to the 60% point and clip the remaining butts.
Dub the thread with olive-brown superfine and build a tapered abdomen from the tail base to the 75% point.
Overlap the thread back onto the abdomen, then tie in a dozen dark dun spade hackle fibers by their butts at the front of the abdomen and clip the butts flush.
Dub thinly with gray beaver, starting at the rear of the index point, work back to the wingcase base and forward again to form a ball-shaped thorax.
Pull the dun fibers forward over the top of the thorax as a wingcase and tie them down at the index point.
Pull half of the remaining fiber tips back along the far side of the hook and bind them with two tight turns.
Pull the other half back along the near side the same way, keeping the fibers along the sides of the hook as legs.
Build a smooth thread head and whip finish at the index point.
Trim the legs to the length of the wingcase and the tail to about half a shank. The finished Barr Emerger.
